vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: customer-service-reply
Version: 1.1.0

The skill is a template generator for customer service replies, providing scripts to generate responses for various scenarios like pre-sales, complaints, and refunds. The core logic in `scripts/cs.sh` is a clean Python script that processes input arguments and prints formatted text to the console without any network calls, file system modifications, or execution of external commands. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions match its stated purpose (generating customer-service reply templates) but a pre-scan found unicode control characters in the SKILL.md (a common prompt-injection signal), so review/sandboxing is recommended before use.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, SKILL.md, tips.md, and scripts/cs.sh all align: the skill generates customer-service reply templates and FAQ text locally. The included shell+Python script implements the described commands and there are no unrelated requested credentials, binaries, or config paths.

llm.guidance: The skill appears to do what it says — generate customer-service reply templates locally — and it doesn't request credentials or access external services. However, an automated scan found unicode control characters in SKILL.md (a prompt-injection indicator). Before installing or running scripts: 1) open SKILL.md and scripts/cs.sh in a plain-text editor and look for unexpected invisible characters or hidden instructions (e.g., zero-width spaces, control codes); 2) run the script in an isolated/sandbox environment (no network) and review its output on benign test inputs; 3) avoid providing any credentials or piping sensitive data into the script; 4) if you will let an agent invoke this skill autonomously, consider restricting that capability until you verify the files. If you find hidden/odd content you don't understand, do not run the skill and seek help from someone who can inspect the files byte-for-byte.
llm.findings: [unicode-control-chars] unexpected: Control/unicode invisibles in SKILL.md are not required for a template generator and can be used to conceal instructions or manipulate prompt parsing. This is a sign worth manual inspection of the SKILL.md and any hidden characters.
